note: Which documentation page feeds which shelf. Routing is declared here and reviewed by a person, never guessed by the importer. Hidden Tricks and Prompts are absent on purpose: calling something a non-obvious trick, or a prompt quoted verbatim, asserts something no parser can establish, so those shelves are filled only by reviewed extraction. See AGENTS.md and scripts/route-signals.mjs.
selection: This archive indexes the documentation; it does not mirror it. Importing every page that parses cleanly yields about 616 entries and turns Settings into the largest shelf, most of it option-by-option reference that reads better upstream and would bury 326 community stories. The pages below are the ones that fill a genuine hole in a shelf.

pages.why: Skills held four entries. This is the page that explains what a skill is and how to install, write and scope one.
The first commands anyone runs; nothing in the archive covered getting started.
Install paths per platform, which the CLI reference does not carry.
Working in the CLI day to day, as opposed to the flag-by-flag reference already imported.
An ordered route through Hermes for someone starting out.
What the agent can actually do, in one place.
A complete worked workflow, which is exactly what this shelf is for.
A worked setup for running a specific model, end to end.
How the thing is built, for people extending it.
What runs where; short and load-bearing when something will not start.
Android setup is genuinely non-obvious and is not covered anywhere else in the archive.

skipped.skills: The Skills Hub is client-rendered, but the official Skills System documentation now identifies a public catalogue at https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/api/skills.json (HTTP 200 verified 2026-09-26). This HTML heading importer does not handle that JSON catalogue. Importing its entries needs separate review of attribution, Hermes applicability and repository eligibility; do not bulk-import the catalogue as verified recommendations.
skipped.plugins: Client-rendered for the same reason, with no headings at all in the served HTML.
skipped.user-guide/configuration: 123 sections of option-by-option reference. It belongs upstream, where it is searchable and current.
skipped.user-guide/security: 42 sections of policy reference. Linking to it beats copying it, and a stale security page in an archive is worse than none.
skipped.user-guide/features/context-files: Reference detail already summarised by existing Settings entries.
skipped.user-guide/features/voice-mode: Reference counterpart to the voice-mode guide, which is imported instead.
skipped.integrations/nous-portal: Account and portal reference rather than a workflow.
skipped.reference/faq: 50 short answers; an archive card per FAQ entry adds nothing over the FAQ itself.
skipped.developer-guide/contributing: Contribution process for Hermes Agent itself, not a workflow anyone runs here.
skipped.reference/cli-commands: Already imported by scripts/import-hermes-cli.mjs, which reads its reference table.
